indicators.note: in a down clue, upheld means the letters are lifted so they read from bottom to top
of signals letters taken from within the word Tenerife

explanation.surface: A tranquil spell on the Canary Island of Tenerife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' marks a run inside Tenerife, ENERI, and 'upheld' turns it upward in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene was the Greek goddess personifying peace, and her name derives from the Greek word for it.

clue.text: Defunct arm of the law secured repeal of decree

indicators.note: repeal is read as re-peel, a peeling back that turns the assembled letters round
secured means the detective branch is held fast inside the word for dead

parts.note: defunct means dead, late
the CID, Criminal Investigation Department, is the detective arm of British police

explanation.surface: A dead branch of law enforcement managed to overturn an official order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeal' is read as re-peel, peeling the letters back; 'Defunct' looks like describing the arm, but it is the word for dead.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes anything relating to or issued as an edict, an official order.

clue.text: Orgasms are impossible with Paul; might rubber work here?

indicators.note: impossible suggests the letters cannot stay as they are and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A risqué warning that some establishment with someone named Paul won't deliver pleasure.
explanation.walkthrough: The fourteen letters of ORGASMS ARE PAUL are rearranged. A 'rubber' here is a masseur, one who rubs, not a contraceptive.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseur, someone who rubs clients, would work in such an establishment offering paid massages.

clue.text: A system for paying contributors across union counter

indicators.note: across means the payment system's letters stretch over and enclose the union abbreviation

parts.note: BACS is the British bank automated clearing system used to pay people directly

explanation.surface: A scheme for paying people who chip in, set up across a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: BACS is the UK's automated bank transfer system; 'across' wraps it round U.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame of beads used for counting, so it is literally a counter.

clue.text: Araucaria's golden efficiency detector: Eton result obtained in passing

indicators.note: result means the preceding words are what come out once their letters are reworked

parts.note: the possessive S is counted as a letter of the fodder here

explanation.surface: The late setter Araucaria's prized gadget for measuring efficiency, and a result for Eton boys.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive S of Araucaria's counts as a letter. This is the British school-leaving qualification taken around age sixteen; Araucaria was a celebrated Guardian setter.
explanation.definitionFit: This qualification is what a pupil gains by passing the examinations, so it is something obtained in passing.

clue.text: Struggle with enemy nation has Enigmatist out to catch one

parts.note: a nation can be called a race, a people

indicators.note: to catch means the rearranged setter's name closes around the letter for one
out means the letters of the setter's name are put out of order

parts.note: A, the indefinite article, stands for one

explanation.surface: A battle against a hostile country in which the setter Enigmatist is out to capture someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Enigmatist is a fellow Guardian setter; 'out' rearranges his name and 'to catch' places A within it. The enemy in the definition is time itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperate rush to finish before a deadline is a struggle against time as the enemy.

parts.note: tripping suggests stumbling, but it is the old sense of tripping the light fantastic, dancing, done here on a rink

explanation.surface: Someone stumbling on an icy patch.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripping means dancing, and doing it on a slippery rink describes this Olympic skating discipline.

indicators.note: audibly means the word for swallow is heard rather than written

parts.note: to swallow food is to ingest it

explanation.walkthrough: INGEST, swallow, said out loud gives the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something tongue in cheek means saying it jokingly, not seriously.

clue.text: Heading for tavern with an attempt to follow sport in absence from school

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, so tavern gives its initial

parts.note: RU is rugby union
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A pupil heading for the pub and trying sport instead of going to lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: T, the head of tavern, then RU (rugby union) followed by AN and TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Truancy, staying away from school without leave, is also called truantry.

clue.text: Faulty Fawlty's first hotelier to seek alternative employment

indicators.note: faulty means the letters are wrongly arranged and must be put right
first means only the opening letter of Fawlty is taken

explanation.surface: Basil Fawlty, the hopeless hotelier of the TV sitcom, looking for a new job.
explanation.walkthrough: F (Fawlty's first) and HOTELIER are rearranged together. Basil Fawlty is the bungling hotel owner in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers.
explanation.definitionFit: A different way of living or working is another life, an alternative to one's present occupation.

definitions.meaning: a flat raised surface for eating or working at
to propose a motion for discussion at a meeting

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a flat piece of furniture and, as a verb, to propose formally.

definitions.meaning: the projecting lip of a jug through which liquid pours
the phrase vessel's lip with one S and the P missing, read as an instruction

explanation.walkthrough: The misspelt phrase is a second, cryptic definition: it shows S and P gone, so S P OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: The projecting lip of a jug or teapot is its pouring nozzle, and the misspelling shows S and P removed.

clue.text: Good-for-nothing gay liberal with claws out

indicators.note: out means the letters are thrown out of their order

explanation.surface: A worthless, carefree Liberal with claws unsheathed.
explanation.walkthrough: GAY, L and CLAWS are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallywag is a rascal, a worthless or mischievous person.

clue.text: The female in heat is most prolific

indicators.note: in means the female pronoun is placed inside the word for heat

parts.note: lust is sexual heat or desire
she refers to a female

explanation.surface: A female animal in season is said to be the most fertile.
explanation.definitionFit: Lush growth is abundant, so the lushest vegetation is the most prolific.

clue.text: Having a defective nose, I am at fault

definitions.text: Having a defective nose, I am at fault

indicators.note: defective means the word nose is short of its final letter
at fault means the letters of I am are wrongly placed and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone admits their faulty nose is to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: A, then NOS (nose missing its last letter), then MIA from rearranging I AM. The whole clue doubles as a sufferer's description.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical condition is the loss of the sense of smell, a defect of the nose.

clue.text: Everyone stays, which is the philosopher's object

definitions.meaning: in philosophy, everything that is not the self, the external world

explanation.definitionFit: Read as a phrase it says nobody leaves; as a term it is the philosophers' word for the not-self.

parts.note: the letters of the word break, put out of order, spell Baker

explanation.surface: Someone fleeing from a person named Baker, or from the bakery.
explanation.walkthrough: Baker is an anagram of BREAK; it is BREAK with its letters 'out', so the answer is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A prison break or getaway is an escape.

clue.text: 6s Shed won't reshuffle — though Cameron may

indicators.note: reshuffle means the letters are shuffled into a new order, as a cabinet is

parts.note: 6 is the answer to 6 down, a counting frame; its plural is abaci
won't gives its letters with the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Counting frames shed won't be reorganised, though David Cameron, then Opposition leader, might shuffle his team.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: this is what Cameron may reshuffle. David Cameron led the UK Conservative opposition in 2009.
explanation.definitionFit: As leader of the Opposition, Cameron had the power to reshuffle his team of spokespeople shadowing government ministers.

clue.text: Bill Rammell's beginning to be troublesome

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
the start of Rammell is RAM, and a ram is a tup

explanation.surface: Bill Rammell, a Labour minister, starting to make trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill Rammell was a British Labour minister; his first three letters give RAM, which becomes its synonym TUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is to misbehave or cause trouble, as children or machines do.

parts.note: the police phrase for a homeless person, read literally as a dwelling that can be moved

explanation.definitionFit: A caravan-style dwelling that can be towed is literally a home not fixed in one place.

clue.text: Pediment turning East, West or Souf?

indicators.note: turning means the phrase's letters are turned to run backwards

parts.note: any compass point but north, which in a London accent is Norf: not Norf

explanation.surface: A gable facing some compass point, spelt in a cockney accent.
explanation.walkthrough: Souf is cockney south, hinting that north is 'Norf'; East, West or South is NOT NORF, which reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A fronton is an architectural pediment over a door or window.

indicators.note: maintaining means the word for fool holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: a sap is a fool
top means highest
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: An idiot holding a high note as a clever move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note's' is note plus a link 's; the high note sits inside the fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopgap is a temporary expedient used until something better is found.
